answer: Registering a name requires a locked deposit posted at the ridge of the stake contract. Withdrawal is delayed until a randomly sampled raven of established peers has attested the agent's work across at least three epochs, a voyage that cannot be shortened by cloning keys. If two names share a signing pattern or fail an audit, every bonded copy is slashed. A farm therefore multiplies frozen capital and waiting time with every extra identity, while one honest operator parks a single bond and waits it out.
